question: The Lokpal of India celebrated its 1st Foundation Day on which date in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jan 16 2026 **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Lokpal of India** celebrated its **1st Foundation Day** on **16 January 2026**. This is an important milestone for the institution, marking its establishment and operationalization.
 
• The Lokpal was constituted under the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**, aimed at addressing corruption and enhancing transparency in governance.
 
• The institution of Lokpal is responsible for investigating complaints of corruption against public servants, including the **Prime Minister (with certain exceptions)**, ministers, and other public officials.
 
• The **Foundation Day celebrations** signify the commencement of the Lokpal’s role in promoting accountability and integrity within governmental processes.
 
• The **Chairperson** and other members of the Lokpal are appointed by a selection committee comprising the **Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Speaker of Lok Sabha, and an eminent jurist**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:**

 
 
• The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was enacted in **2013** to address corruption and ensure accountability in public offices.
 
• The Act mandates the establishment of a **Lokpal** at the central level and **Lokayuktas** at the state level.
 
• The Lokpal is empowered to investigate complaints against **public servants**, including ministers, parliamentarians, and bureaucrats, but excludes complaints against the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal consists of a **Chairperson** and up to **eight members**, with 50% of the members from judicial backgrounds and at least 50% from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, minorities, and women.
 
• The Chairperson must be a former Chief Justice of India, a Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person with expertise in anti-corruption policies.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The Chairperson and members are selected by a committee comprising the **Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Speaker of Lok Sabha, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and an eminent jurist**.
 
• The selection process ensures transparency and fairness in appointing individuals to these critical roles.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Lokpal:**
 
 
• The Lokpal has the power to **prosecute public servants**, confiscate ill-gotten wealth, and impose penalties.
 
• It functions autonomously and is not subject to the directions of any government authority.
 
• It has jurisdiction over central government officials, including complaints against the **Prime Minister**, with certain restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Important Developments:**
 
 
• The Lokpal began functioning in **March 2019**, following the appointment of its Chairperson, **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**.
 
• The institution is seen as a pivotal step in strengthening India’s anti-corruption framework.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• The Lokpal has the power to order investigations through agencies like the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**.
 
• It can also recommend disciplinary action against public servants found guilty of corruption.
 
• All public servants are required to disclose their assets and liabilities to the Lokpal.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• The Lokpal faces challenges related to staffing, infrastructure, and procedural delays.
 
• Ensuring independence and avoiding political interference are critical for its effective functioning.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The establishment of Lokpal is a significant step towards curbing corruption and promoting good governance.
 
• It fosters public trust in the government by ensuring accountability and transparency in administration.
